question.text: 'Himalaya Opportunities' Cat II AIF is considering reinvesting sale proceeds from one exited investment into a new deal. The chapter's guidance on alignment-of-interest states that reinvestment:

answer.text: Can be done for any amount as long as the manager approves
Requires SEBI pre-approval for amounts above INR 100 crore
Cannot exceed the capital invested (or acquisition price) in the asset that gave rise to the income distribution subject to reinvestment
Must be communicated to investors only after the reinvestment is completed

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.8 (Role of Human Capital), if the Manager is retaining sales proceeds for reinvestment, investors should be communicated conditions upfront and subject to quantitative/time limitations. Reinvestment cannot exceed the capital invested (or acquisition price) in the asset that gave rise to the income distribution subject to reinvestment. The Trap: Option A ignores the cap. Option C invents SEBI pre-approval. Option D violates the pre-disclosure duty. Cross-Exam Context: Reinvestment/recycling provisions are heavily negotiated in PPMs; tested in XIX-A and XIX-C. Manager's Pro-Tip: The acquisition-price cap is tight — even modest value creation pre-exit means the reinvestment can't absorb the full proceeds. Plan distributions to LPs for the uplift portion.
